--- title: "[SmoothBasis]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-abc}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Abstract base class for all smooth basis types. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L11-L162){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python SmoothBasis() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Every smooth term in a GAM — a thin plate spline, a cubic regression spline, a P-spline, a Gaussian process smooth, and so on — is represented internally as a linear basis expansion `f(x) = B(x) @ beta` together with a quadratic roughness penalty `beta.T @ S @ beta`. This class fixes the contract that every basis type must satisfy so that the fitting machinery (penalized least squares, smoothing-parameter selection, prediction) can treat all basis types uniformly. Concrete subclasses differ only in how `B` and `S` are constructed, not in how they are consumed. Subclasses must implement `fit()`, `basis_matrix()`, `penalty_matrix()`, `null_space_dimension()`, and the `n_basis` property. The typical workflow is:: basis = MyBasis(k=10) basis.fit(x_train) B_train = basis.basis_matrix(x_train) # (n_train, k) B_new = basis.basis_matrix(x_new) # (n_new, k) S = basis.penalty_matrix() # (k, k) ::: ## Notes {.doc-notes} A penalized basis decomposes its `k` basis functions into an unpenalized *null space* of dimension `M` (typically low-order polynomials, for which the penalty contributes nothing — e.g. a straight line has zero roughness under a second-derivative penalty) and a penalized *range space* of dimension `k - M`. The total penalty for smoothing parameter `lambda` is $$ \lambda \, \boldsymbol{\beta}^\top \mathbf{S} \boldsymbol{\beta}, $$ where `S` is symmetric positive semi-definite with `null_space_dimension()` zero eigenvalues. Basis types built on this contract may additionally supply identifiability constraints (via `identifiability_constraints()`) when the raw basis is not full rank on its own — for example when several smooth terms share an intercept and must each be constrained to have mean zero over the training data. ## Examples {.doc-examples} Any concrete subclass follows this pattern: ::: {#d8a8f270 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from whittaker.smooths import TPRS rng = np.random.default_rng(0) x = rng.uniform(0, 1, 100) basis = TPRS(k=10).fit(x) B = basis.basis_matrix(x) S = basis.penalty_matrix() B.shape, S.shape ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` ((100, 10), (10, 10)) ``` ::: ::: ## Attributes {.doc-attributes}
Name Description
is_fitted `True` after `fit()` has been called.
n_basis Number of basis functions k.
### [is_fitted]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} `True` after `fit()` has been called. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [is_fitted]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [bool]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ### [n_basis]{.doc-object-name .doc-attribute .doc-label .doc-label-property} ::: {.doc-subject} Number of basis functions k. ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-attribute} [n_basis]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
basis_matrix() Evaluate basis functions at `x`.
fit() Fit the basis to training data.
identifiability_constraints() Return constraint matrix C such that `C @ β = 0`, or `None`.
null_space_dimension() Return the dimension M of the penalty null space.
penalty_matrix() Return the `(k, k)` penalty matrix S.
### [basis_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Evaluate basis functions at `x`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L88-L103){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python basis_matrix(x) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Covariate values. Shape `(n,)` for univariate or `(n, d)` for multivariate. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Design matrix of shape `(n, k)` where `k = self.n_basis`. ::: ### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the basis to training data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L68-L86){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(x) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Stores any parameters required for later calls to `basis_matrix()` (e.g. knot locations, transformation matrices). ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [x]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [NDArray]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Training covariates. Shape `(n,)` for univariate smooths or `(n, d)` for multivariate smooths. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [self]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Returns the instance to allow method chaining. ::: ### [identifiability_constraints()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return constraint matrix C such that `C @ β = 0`, or `None`. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L123-L129){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python identifiability_constraints() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Subclasses may override this to supply sum-to-zero or other identifiability constraints for use during model fitting. ::: ### [null_space_dimension()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the dimension M of the penalty null space. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L114-L121){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python null_space_dimension() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The first M columns of the basis matrix correspond to the unpenalized polynomial null space. ::: ### [penalty_matrix()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Return the `(k, k)` penalty matrix S. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/whittaker/blob/main/whittaker/smooths/base.py#L105-L112){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python penalty_matrix() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} The total penalty contribution for smoothing parameter λ is `λ * β @ S @ β`. :::
